etymologies.etymologyHTML: From an ellipsis of Middle English it may be, equivalent to may +‎ be. Compare mayhap.

definitions.definition: (as a pro-sentence) Perhaps that is true (expressing no commitment to a decision or a neutral viewpoint to a statement).

quote.text:
Okay. See you later, maybe. — Maybe I’ll see you later.
Audio (US):(file)

quote.citation: 1687, John Dryden, The Hind and the Panther, part III line 294:
quote.text: Then add those may-be years thou hast to live

definitions.definition: (informal) An answer that shows neither agreement nor disagreement.
(informal) A future event that may or may not happen.
